title: Summit Leaders: The 7 Peaks Challenge
description: Climb the world's greatest peaks and prove your leadership! Navigate crises, earn coins, complete Leadership Challenges, and develop 8 core traits — Self-Awareness, Communication, Teamwork, Decisiveness, Resilience, Vision, Confidence, and Integrity. Race 3 AI rivals to summit Mt. Everest first!

storybook_pages.title: The 7 Peaks Challenge Begins!
storybook_pages.text: Welcome, young leader! You've been chosen to lead your team on the greatest mountaineering challenge ever — summit all 7 of the world's most iconic peaks. Along the way you'll face Leadership Challenges, team crises, and critical decisions that reveal what kind of leader you truly are.

storybook_pages.title: Your Leadership Journey
storybook_pages.text: As you climb, you'll earn Gold (5 pts), Silver (2 pts), and Bronze (1 pt) coins. Land on Leadership Challenge spaces (♦) to answer scenario questions and earn trait badges. Visit Summit spaces (★) to collect bonus coins when you reach each peak!

storybook_pages.title: 3 AI Rivals Await
storybook_pages.text: Three rival leaders — the bold Visionary, the calculating Strategist, and the charming Diplomat — are racing you to the top. Use Block Cards, Deal Cards, and Comeback Cards to gain an edge. The leader with the most points and summit badges wins!

how_to_play: Roll the dice and move around the 40-space board. Each full lap earns you Bronze coins.
Land on a Leadership Challenge space (♦) to answer a scenario — correct answers earn more coins and boost your leadership traits.
Land on a Crisis space (⚡) to face an unexpected challenge — manage it wisely to minimize coin loss.
Visit Rest & Recover spaces (⛺) to recharge and earn bonus trait points.
Reach a Summit space (★) to claim that peak and earn Gold coins. First to each summit gets the most!
Use Deal Cards to negotiate with rivals, Block Cards to slow them down, and Comeback Cards if you fall behind.
The player with the highest total score (coins + trait badges + summits) at Mt. Everest wins!

start.message: Base Camp! Collect 2 Bronze coins and set off on your leadership journey! 🏕️

rest.message: Rest & Recover! Your team recharges. Earn a Silver coin and boost your Resilience and Confidence! ⛺

treasure.message: SUMMIT REACHED! ★ You've conquered this peak! Earn a Gold coin and boost your Vision and Confidence!

finish.message: 🏔️ MT. EVEREST SUMMIT! You've reached the top of the world! This is true leadership!

shop_items.label: Team Rope
shop_items.description: A rope that links your team — strengthen Teamwork and Resilience together.

shop_items.label: Leadership Compass
shop_items.description: Never lose direction. Boost your Vision and Decisiveness.

shop_items.label: Self-Reflection Journal
shop_items.description: Write your thoughts and grow your Self-Awareness and Integrity.

shop_items.label: Team Radio
shop_items.description: Stay connected with your team at all times. Boost Communication.

challenge.question: FINAL SUMMIT CHALLENGE: You're 200m from Everest's summit. A rival team member calls for help — injured. Helping costs you the race. What kind of leader are you?
options: Stops immediately — people always come before trophies
Helps them call rescue while continuing
Delegates to team members while you push for summit
Signals for help and trusts rescue protocols
option_explanations: Pure humanity over ambition. Strongest integrity signal — this choice defines legacy leaders.
Balanced leadership: you act AND lead. High integrity with strategic thinking.
Delegation is leadership too — trusting your team is a mark of maturity.
Systems thinking: trusting processes and protocols keeps everyone safer.
challenge.success_message: SUMMIT LEADER! Every choice here shows a different kind of leadership strength. Reflect on what drives you.
challenge.explanation: In real leadership, ethical dilemmas rarely have one right answer. What matters is your reasoning, your values, and what you're willing to stand for.

power_ups.label: Block Card
power_ups.description: Block a rival from moving this turn — use it strategically!

power_ups.label: Deal Card
power_ups.description: Negotiate with a rival — trade coins or swap positions.

power_ups.label: Comeback Card
power_ups.description: If you're last place, move forward 4 extra spaces. The underdog bonus!

ai_competitors.name: The Visionary
ai_competitors.description: Always looks at the big picture. Bold moves, takes risks on summits.

ai_competitors.name: The Strategist
ai_competitors.description: Calculates every move. Maximises coin efficiency and avoids crises.

ai_competitors.name: The Diplomat
ai_competitors.description: Wins through relationships. Uses Deal Cards to trade and cooperate.

card_pool.name: Visionary Spark
card_pool.knowledge: Leaders with clear vision outperform others by 43% (Gallup). Vision isn't prediction — it's choosing direction before the path is obvious.

card_pool.name: Team Synergy
card_pool.knowledge: Lencioni's Five Dysfunctions shows trust is the foundation of high performance. High-trust teams are 50% more productive than low-trust ones.

card_pool.name: Resilience Boost
card_pool.knowledge: Carol Dweck's research: resilient people treat setbacks as information, not failure. Resilience is a learned skill, not a fixed trait.

card_pool.name: Decisive Moment
card_pool.knowledge: Bezos's 'two-way door' rule: fast decisions are safe to reverse. Only truly irreversible choices deserve slow, deep analysis.

card_pool.name: Integrity Shield
card_pool.knowledge: Warren Buffett: 'It takes 20 years to build a reputation and 5 minutes to ruin it.' Integrity compounds silently — until it doesn't.

card_pool.name: Summit Compass
card_pool.knowledge: Tasha Eurich: self-aware leaders are 79% more likely to perform well. Knowing your blind spots is the real competitive edge.

evt_self_awareness_1.title: Self-Awareness Circle
evt_self_awareness_1.description: Your team gathers to share honest feedback about each other. You listen carefully and reflect.

choices.label: Listen carefully and take notes on the feedback
choices.outcome: You listen without defensiveness and learn something valuable. +10 Self-Awareness!

choices.label: Explain your perspective and defend your choices
choices.outcome: You defended yourself but missed an opportunity for self-growth. +3 Self-Awareness.

evt_team_rally.title: Team Rally Before the Climb!
evt_team_rally.description: Your team is nervous about the challenging route ahead. As the leader, you must rally their spirits.

choices.label: Share your vision of reaching the summit together
choices.outcome: Your passionate speech energises the team! Everyone moves forward with renewed purpose.

choices.label: Give a practical briefing on the route plan
choices.outcome: Clear and practical — the team knows exactly what to do. Good leadership!

evt_wisdom_1.title: Wilderness Wisdom 📖
evt_wisdom_1.description: An experienced mountain guide shares a leadership lesson: 'A leader sets the example, not just the direction.'

choices.label: Take the first step into the hardest trail section yourself
choices.outcome: You lead by example. The team follows your lead with confidence.

choices.label: Share this lesson with your whole team
choices.outcome: Your team loves it! Sharing knowledge strengthens the whole group.

evt_skill_challenge_1.title: Trail Crossing Challenge
evt_skill_challenge_1.description: The path splits. You must calculate which route is shorter and safer for your team.

choices.label: Study the map carefully before choosing the route
choices.outcome: Your careful analysis pays off — you choose the safer, faster route!

choices.label: Ask your team for input before deciding
choices.outcome: Great collaborative decision! Everyone feels heard and the team bonds over this.

evt_teamwork_1.title: Team Discussion: Route Planning
evt_teamwork_1.description: Two team members disagree — one wants speed, the other wants safety. You must decide.

choices.label: Find a middle-ground route that balances speed and safety
choices.outcome: Excellent mediation! Both team members feel respected and you move forward united.

choices.label: Make the call yourself as the leader
choices.outcome: Decision made, but some team members feel left out. Work on inclusive leadership.

evt_skill_training.title: Skill Training Session
evt_skill_training.description: You find an expert coach willing to train your team for 30 minutes.

choices.label: Train together as a team
choices.outcome: Shared struggle builds shared strength! The whole team levels up.

choices.label: Focus on your own weakest skill
choices.outcome: You know your gaps and work on them. Self-improvement is a leader's strength.

evt_peer_learning.title: Learning From a Peer
evt_peer_learning.description: A rival leader offers to share their climbing technique with you.

choices.label: Accept eagerly and share your techniques too
choices.outcome: Mutual learning! Both of you grow stronger. Integrity and generosity pay off.

choices.label: Politely decline — protect your competitive advantage
choices.outcome: You stayed competitive, but missed a chance to grow through collaboration.

evt_rivalry.title: Rivalry Encounter
evt_rivalry.description: A rival team is blocking your path at a narrow trail section!

choices.label: Negotiate a deal — offer to share your rest spot later
choices.outcome: Smart diplomacy! You pass and even make a useful ally for later.

choices.label: Find an alternate route around them
choices.outcome: Adaptable thinking! You take a detour but keep your momentum going.

evt_resilience_1.title: After the Setback
evt_resilience_1.description: Your team failed a tough section and morale is at an all-time low. Three members want to quit.

choices.label: Share a personal failure story and how you bounced back
choices.outcome: Your vulnerability and honesty inspire the team. Morale soars!

choices.label: Remind them of the summit goal and push forward
choices.outcome: The vision of the summit pulls the team through. Forward momentum restored!

evt_team_bonding.title: Team Bonding Night at Camp
evt_team_bonding.description: You have an evening to strengthen team bonds before the hardest section tomorrow.

choices.label: Sit around the fire and share personal stories
choices.outcome: Deep connection builds! Your team becomes more than just climbers — you're a unit.

choices.label: Use the time to plan tomorrow's route together
choices.outcome: Strategic and practical! The team is aligned and ready for the challenge.

evt_confidence_1.title: Confidence Workshop
evt_confidence_1.description: You're asked to lead a 5-minute presentation at high camp in front of all teams.

choices.label: Volunteer immediately and speak confidently
choices.outcome: Your bold step inspires everyone! Speaking up builds confidence exponentially.

choices.label: Ask for 2 minutes to prepare, then present
choices.outcome: Well-prepared and thoughtful! Knowing when to prepare is also strong leadership.

evt_wisdom_2.title: High Altitude Wisdom 📖
evt_wisdom_2.description: You find a note from a legendary climber: 'The summit is what drives us, but the climb itself is what matters.'

choices.label: Reflect deeply and share this insight with your team
choices.outcome: This shifts your perspective. You lead with more depth and purpose.

choices.label: Appreciate it, but stay focused on reaching the summit
choices.outcome: Goal-focused and determined. Your drive keeps the team moving forward.

evt_final_briefing.title: Final Zone Briefing
evt_final_briefing.description: You're in the final zone! Mt. Everest is ahead. You call an emergency team meeting.

choices.label: Lay out a detailed strategic plan for the final push
choices.outcome: Your team goes into the final leg with full clarity and confidence.

choices.label: Ask each team member to share their best idea
choices.outcome: Empowering others is true leadership. Your team rises to the occasion!

evt_integrity_2.title: The Integrity Moment
evt_integrity_2.description: You discover a shortcut that skips a difficult section — but rules say all teams must complete the full route.

choices.label: Refuse the shortcut — complete the full route with integrity
choices.outcome: INTEGRITY IN ACTION! You choose what's right over what's easy. Massive respect earned!

choices.label: Take the shortcut — everyone else might too
choices.outcome: You gained time but lost something more important. Integrity is built in moments like these.

evt_deal_making.title: Deal Making with Rivals
evt_deal_making.description: Two rival teams offer you a deal: combine resources to tackle the final stretch together.

choices.label: Accept — share resources and summit together
choices.outcome: Collaboration over competition! You all reach the summit zone stronger.

choices.label: Decline — you'll make it on your own
choices.outcome: Independent and determined. Your self-reliance is impressive.

evt_comeback.title: The Comeback Trail 🔥
evt_comeback.description: You've fallen behind in points. But you spot an opportunity to make a dramatic comeback!

choices.label: Push with everything you have — surge forward!
choices.outcome: COMEBACK! You surge forward. Never count a true leader out! +3 Bronze coins.

choices.label: Keep your steady pace — consistency wins
choices.outcome: Steady as the mountain itself. Your consistent leadership is a strength.

evt_crisis_altitude.title: ⚡ Crisis: Altitude Sickness!
evt_crisis_altitude.description: Two team members show signs of altitude sickness. You must decide how to respond fast.

choices.label: Descend 100m with sick members and help them recover
choices.outcome: You lose a coin but gain massive respect. They recover and rejoin the climb.

choices.label: Give them extra water and push through slowly
choices.outcome: It works but barely. You lose 2 Bronze coins in emergency supplies.

evt_crisis_storm.title: ⚡ Crisis: Alpine Storm!
evt_crisis_storm.description: A sudden storm hits! You must find shelter fast or risk losing precious resources.

choices.label: Stop and set up your emergency tent immediately
choices.outcome: Good call! You lose a Bronze coin in setup time but everyone is safe.

choices.label: Push hard to reach the established camp before it worsens
choices.outcome: You make it but the effort cost 2 Bronze coins. Brave but risky!

evt_crisis_equipment.title: ⚡ Crisis: Equipment Failure!
evt_crisis_equipment.description: Critical climbing equipment has failed. You must improvise or lose significant time.

choices.label: Improvise a solution with what you have
choices.outcome: MacGyver-level resourcefulness! -1 Bronze coin cost. Impressive!

choices.label: Request support from base camp — wait for replacement gear
choices.outcome: Help arrives but costs 1 Silver coin and valuable time.

evt_crisis_final.title: ⚡ Final Crisis: Sudden Whiteout!
evt_crisis_final.description: A severe whiteout makes navigation impossible. Your GPS fails. What now?

choices.label: Use compass and map — navigate by fundamentals
choices.outcome: Old-school skill saves the day! -1 Bronze coin but you navigate safely.

choices.label: Stop, secure the team, and wait for visibility
choices.outcome: Patient and safe — but waiting costs a Silver coin.

evt_lc_communication_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Communication
evt_lc_communication_1.description: A team member is struggling but won't speak up. How do you create a safe space for them?

choices.label: Speak privately: 'I noticed you seemed quiet — I'm here if you want to talk'
choices.outcome: EXCELLENT! Private, empathetic check-ins are the hallmark of a great communicator. +15 Communication! 🏅

choices.label: Call them out in front of the group so everyone can help
choices.outcome: Leaders create psychological safety — people open up when they feel safe, not pressured.

choices.label: Ignore it — they'll speak up when they're ready
choices.outcome: Great leaders notice and address problems early, not wait for them to escalate.

choices.label: Tell them they need to communicate better or they're off the team
choices.outcome: Threats destroy trust. Psychological safety is the foundation of great team communication.

evt_lc_self_awareness_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Self-Awareness
evt_lc_self_awareness_1.description: Your team gives you difficult feedback: 'You make decisions too fast without asking us.'

choices.label: 'Thank you for telling me — I'll work on including you more in decisions'
choices.outcome: Self-aware leaders welcome feedback! That's the first step to growth. +15 Self-Awareness! 🏅

choices.label: 'I'm the leader — I need to make quick decisions to keep us moving'
choices.outcome: Speed matters, but so does inclusion. The best leaders balance both.

choices.label: 'I disagree — I always explain my reasoning afterwards'
choices.outcome: Explaining after is not the same as including before. Self-awareness means seeing our own blind spots.

choices.label: 'If you don't like how I lead, you can find another team'
choices.outcome: Dismissing feedback is the opposite of self-awareness. Leaders grow by listening.

evt_lc_decisiveness_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Decisiveness
evt_lc_decisiveness_1.description: The weather is turning dangerous. A 60% chance of worsening storm. Your team is divided.

choices.label: Make the safest call (turn back), explain clearly, and commit to the decision
choices.outcome: Decisive AND safe! Great leaders make the hard call and own it. +15 Decisiveness! 🏅

choices.label: Let the team vote and go with whatever they decide
choices.outcome: Teams need leaders who make calls, not just pass decisions back to the group.

choices.label: Wait 2 hours to see if the storm passes before deciding
choices.outcome: Waiting too long in a crisis is itself a decision — and often the wrong one.

choices.label: Push through because leaders never give up
choices.outcome: Persistence is admirable, but knowing when to retreat is a sign of wisdom, not weakness.

evt_lc_vision_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Vision
evt_lc_vision_1.description: Your team is exhausted and asking 'Why are we doing this?' How do you respond?

choices.label: 'Every peak we summit proves we can do hard things — this skill carries us through life!'
choices.outcome: VISIONARY! Connecting today's struggle to tomorrow's growth is pure leadership gold. +15 Vision! 🏅

choices.label: 'Because we signed up for this and we can't quit now'
choices.outcome: Commitment matters, but great leaders inspire through purpose, not just obligation.

choices.label: 'The prize money at the end is worth it'
choices.outcome: External rewards motivate short-term. Vision creates lasting drive.

choices.label: 'Because I said so — I'm the leader'
choices.outcome: Authority without inspiration is just control. Leaders earn followership through vision.

evt_lc_integrity_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Integrity
evt_lc_integrity_1.description: You could log slightly exaggerated progress data to look better in rankings — nobody would know.

choices.label: Log accurate numbers — your real progress is something to be proud of
choices.outcome: INTEGRITY MASTER! You chose honesty when no one was watching. That's the true test. +20 Integrity! 🏅

choices.label: Exaggerate slightly — everyone does it and it's a minor thing
choices.outcome: Small lies build habits. True leaders maintain integrity even in tiny moments.

choices.label: Ask your team whether to do it so the decision is shared
choices.outcome: Don't share the burden of unethical decisions. Leaders own their integrity personally.

choices.label: Skip the log entirely to avoid the dilemma
choices.outcome: Avoiding accountability is not integrity — it's avoidance. Face it with honesty.

evt_lc_resilience_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Resilience
evt_lc_resilience_1.description: After a terrible setback that destroys 2 days of progress, your team is devastated.

choices.label: Acknowledge how hard this feels, then calmly discuss how to move forward step by step
choices.outcome: TRUE RESILIENCE! Acknowledging pain AND moving forward — that's how leaders build unbreakable teams. +15 Resilience! 🏅

choices.label: Immediately start planning the recovery — no time to feel bad
choices.outcome: Action matters, but ignoring emotions creates hidden problems. Acknowledge, then act.

choices.label: Blame the circumstances so the team doesn't feel like failures
choices.outcome: Blame teaches nothing. Ownership and learning from failure is true resilience.

choices.label: Tell everyone to toughen up — setbacks are part of the journey
choices.outcome: Resilience isn't about ignoring pain — it's about feeling it and rising anyway.

evt_lc_teamwork_1.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Teamwork
evt_lc_teamwork_1.description: Your strongest climber wants to go ahead alone. The rest of your team would be left behind.

choices.label: 'We climb together or not at all — our strength is in our unity, not individual speed'
choices.outcome: TEAM FIRST! The greatest summits are shared. You just showed what true leadership looks like. +15 Teamwork! 🏅

choices.label: 'Okay, go ahead — that's fair, you've worked hard'
choices.outcome: Letting one person break from the team undermines cohesion. Teamwork means no one is left behind.

choices.label: 'Fine, but you'll help the rest of us with your summit experience afterward'
choices.outcome: A compromise, but real teams don't split in the hardest moments.

choices.label: 'Everyone can do what they want — I'll just focus on myself'
choices.outcome: A leader who abandons the team's unity has lost their most important role.

evt_lc_communication_2.title: ♦ Leadership Challenge: Advanced Communication
evt_lc_communication_2.description: You must explain a complex 3-step strategy to your exhausted, stressed team before the final push.

choices.label: Use simple language, check understanding after each step, and invite questions
choices.outcome: MASTER COMMUNICATOR! Clear, checked, and inclusive communication under pressure. +15 Communication! 🏅

choices.label: Write it down in full detail and hand out printed instructions
choices.outcome: Written details help, but exhausted climbers need spoken, human communication.

choices.label: Explain everything at once quickly so they can rest sooner
choices.outcome: Speed over clarity causes confusion. Great communicators check for understanding.

choices.label: Just tell them what to do — details confuse tired people
choices.outcome: Oversimplifying loses critical information. Leaders adapt their communication style, not their content.

player_roles.name: The Visionary
player_roles.description: You see far beyond the current moment. Your strength is inspiring others with big-picture thinking.

player_roles.name: The Strategist
player_roles.description: You think several moves ahead. Efficient, analytical, and always prepared.

player_roles.name: The Diplomat
player_roles.description: You bring people together. A natural communicator who resolves conflict with grace.

player_roles.name: The Innovator
player_roles.description: You solve problems in creative ways. Adaptable, resilient, and full of energy.

glossary_terms.definition: A clear, compelling picture of where a leader wants to take their team or organisation in the future.
glossary_terms.example: In the game, activating Visionary Spark boosts your vision stat and unlocks better team decisions.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Vision = the destination before the map exists.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: James Collins and Jerry Porras in 'Built to Last' (1994) found visionary companies outperformed the market by 6× over 50 years. Vision works because it aligns dispersed teams without constant instruction — everyone moves toward the same north star independently. Gallup research shows leaders who articulate clear vision have teams with 43% higher engagement.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Martin Luther King Jr. didn't say 'I have a strategic plan.' He said 'I have a dream.' The specificity and emotionality of his vision mobilised a movement. JFK's 1961 declaration 'we will put a man on the moon by the end of the decade' gave NASA a deadline and a vivid mental image — both proven techniques for vision effectiveness.

glossary_terms.definition: The behavioural patterns, relationships, and communication styles that affect how a team functions together.
glossary_terms.example: The Team Synergy card in the game models how aligned, high-trust teams massively amplify output.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Dynamics = the invisible force that either multiplies or divides team output.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Bruce Tuckman's 1965 model describes teams progressing through Forming (polite, figuring each other out), Storming (conflict as roles are contested), Norming (establishing working agreements), and Performing (high-trust, high-output). Leaders who understand this model accelerate the journey from Forming to Performing. Most teams get stuck in Storming.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Google's Project Aristotle spent 2 years analysing 180 teams to find what makes teams effective. The answer wasn't who was on the team but how the team interacted. The single strongest predictor was psychological safety — whether team members felt safe to take risks. IQ of individuals was nearly irrelevant.

glossary_terms.definition: The capacity to absorb setbacks, adapt quickly, and emerge from adversity without losing momentum or confidence.
glossary_terms.example: Resilience Boost cards regenerate your resilience stat, letting you recover faster from negative events.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Resilience = elastic, not rigid. It bends but doesn't break.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Nassim Taleb distinguishes fragile (breaks under stress), robust (resists stress), and antifragile (gets stronger under stress). The best leaders are antifragile: they use crises to accelerate learning. Carol Dweck's growth mindset research shows resilience is learnable — people who believe abilities are fixed become more fragile under failure, while those who believe in growth become more resilient.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison on Robben Island, often in a concrete cell smaller than a car park space. Rather than becoming bitter, he used the time to study, build relationships with guards, and develop the political philosophy and emotional steadiness that made his presidency transformational. Resilience at the highest possible level.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting a course of action from alternatives, balancing incomplete information, time pressure, and consequences.
glossary_terms.example: The Decisive Moment card locks until you're 50% through the climb — symbolising that better decisions come with experience.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Decisions = choosing where to plant the seed, knowing you can't predict the harvest.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Daniel Kahneman's System 1 (fast, intuitive) and System 2 (slow, deliberate) thinking describes two modes leaders use. High-stakes decisions require System 2: deliberate analysis with structured frameworks. Jeff Bezos distinguishes 'two-way door' decisions (reversible, make them fast) from 'one-way door' decisions (irreversible, make them slowly and carefully).
glossary_terms.real_world_example: In the 2013 Amazon Prime Air announcement, Bezos used a two-way door decision — announcing drone delivery before it was technically possible to test public and regulatory appetite. It cost little and the information gathered was valuable. By contrast, when AWS was launched in 2006, it was an irreversible multi-billion dollar infrastructure commitment that required deep, slow deliberation.

glossary_terms.definition: Consistently acting in alignment with stated values, especially when no one is watching and when it is costly to do so.
glossary_terms.example: The Integrity Shield card passively buffs your integrity stat for a round — modelling how consistent behaviour builds trust over time.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Integrity = do the same thing when watched and unwatched.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Behavioural economist Dan Ariely found that most people don't cheat maximally even when they could — but almost everyone cheats a little. The key ethical muscle is the gap between 'what I'd do if no one knew' and 'what I do when watched'. Leaders with integrity reduce that gap to near zero. Frances Frei at Harvard argues integrity is the foundation of trust: without it, no other quality matters.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: When Malden Mills factory burned down in 1995, CEO Aaron Feuerstein chose to pay his 3,000 employees full wages and benefits for 3 months while rebuilding. It cost $25M — nearly bankrupting him. He said: 'I have a responsibility to the worker, both blue-collar and white-collar.' The employees returned with extraordinary loyalty and productivity.

glossary_terms.definition: Accurate understanding of your own strengths, weaknesses, values, emotional reactions, and how others perceive you.
glossary_terms.example: The Summit Compass card — which boosts all traits equally — represents the power of self-awareness to improve in every dimension simultaneously.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Self-awareness = knowing your own map well enough to navigate for others.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Tasha Eurich's research with 5,000 participants found only 10–15% of people are genuinely self-aware, despite 95% believing they are. Self-awareness has two forms: internal (knowing your own values and reactions) and external (knowing how others see you). Leaders tend to develop internal awareness but neglect external — creating blind spots that derail careers. 360-degree feedback is designed to close this gap.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Ray Dalio at Bridgewater made radical transparency and self-awareness core principles: all meetings are recorded, all feedback is logged, and everyone's 'believability' scores are tracked publicly. He credits this relentless self-awareness culture as the reason Bridgewater became the world's largest hedge fund — and the reason many talented people choose not to work there.

glossary_terms.definition: The deliberate transmission of information, meaning, and intent across different people, contexts, and channels.
glossary_terms.example: Team Synergy and Visionary Spark both boost communication — because neither vision nor teamwork works without clear signals.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Communication = the message received, not the message sent.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Albert Mehrabian's famous 7-38-55 rule (often misquoted) found that in face-to-face communication of emotional content, 7% comes from words, 38% from tone of voice, 55% from body language. The implication isn't that words don't matter — it's that alignment between words, tone, and body language is critical. Leaders who 'say the right thing' but sound uncertain undermine their own message.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Winston Churchill's 'We shall fight on the beaches' speech (June 1940) came at Britain's darkest hour. Rhetoricians note the power came from simple Anglo-Saxon words, rising cadence, and tricolon structure. Churchill rehearsed speeches for hours. Communication as a strategic weapon won Britain time to survive.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to see beyond immediate problems to identify patterns, anticipate consequences, and position for long-term advantage.
glossary_terms.example: Every major decision on the summit path requires thinking 3–5 moves ahead — the same skill as strategic thinking in real organisations.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Strategy = playing chess, not checkers. Checkers reacts; chess anticipates.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Michael Porter distinguishes operational effectiveness (doing the same things as competitors but better) from strategy (doing different things). Many organisations optimise relentlessly but never ask whether they're optimising the right things. Roger Martin's 'Playing to Win' framework asks two questions: Where will we play? How will we win? Leaders who cannot answer both clearly are managing, not strategising.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Netflix's 2007 strategic decision to invest in streaming before it was economically obvious — while its DVD-by-mail business was still dominant — is a textbook case. CEO Reed Hastings called it 'cannibalising ourselves before someone else does.' By the time competitors reacted, Netflix had a 5-year head start in original content and global scale.

transfer_exercises.real_world: Before your next team meeting, write down 3 long-term outcomes you want—then map today's agenda to those outcomes.
transfer_exercises.challenge: This week: identify one decision at work/school where you can apply 'second-order thinking'—what happens after the immediate result?

transfer_exercises.game_context: You navigated setbacks and kept your team's morale intact.
transfer_exercises.real_world: After your next failure or setback, write a 3-sentence 'post-mortem': what happened, what you learned, what you'll do differently.
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice Bezos's 'two-way door' test: which decisions this week are reversible? Make those fast. Slow down only on irreversible ones.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Your leadership style shifted as team dynamics changed.
transfer_exercises.real_world: This week, ask someone on your team for direct feedback on one recent decision you made.
transfer_exercises.challenge: Try running a 5-minute 'pre-mortem' before your next big decision: imagine it failed—what went wrong?
